title: Benign text that uses format characters meaningfully
summary: Ordinary text that uses ZWJ (emoji family sequence), ZWNJ (Persian), variation selector U+FE0F, a leading BOM and NBSP between a number and its unit, with no credential in it.
rationale: These code points carry meaning in ordinary text, which is why stripping every invisible character from an input is not assumed safe: it would change a ZWJ emoji sequence into separate emoji and a Persian word. A format character is not evidence of a credential.
unscopedReason: Input-domain control about text, not about any one credential family.

expectation.rationale: Project policy: text with format characters and no credential-grammar value is not a credential; the fixtures carry no spans. A decoder succeeding or a high-entropy look does not make a value a secret.

sources.supports: U+FEFF in UTF-8 is the bytes EF BB BF and, away from the start of a stream, is a ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE, not a signature.
sources.locator: 'What should I do with U+FEFF in the middle of a file?' and 'Can a UTF-8 data stream contain the BOM character?'

sources.supports: Revision 58 (Unicode 18.0.0): defines NFC, NFD, NFKC and NFKD; ASCII-only text is unchanged by every form. Does not state that normalization removes zero-width or format characters.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Research for #96 (parent #92). Synthetic fixtures only; input facts and expectations live here, while stream APIs, limits, actual output and rejection assertions belong to downstream engine and product regression populations.
